title: Benchmark report charts scratchpad (latency/$ + latency + cost views)
content:
Working scratchpad for chart ideas + rough sketches for the public benchmark report + interactive page.

Primary narrative we’re trying to show (in charts):
- It’s not just “fast,” it’s “fast for the cost” (latency per dollar / latency per $).
- Performance is consistent across regions (not a single cherry-picked run).
- Tail latency matters in production (p95), not just average.
- Readers can map results to their workload via toggles (context length, output length, concurrency).

------------------------------------------------------------
0) Definitions (keep consistent across all visuals)
- latency/$ (a.k.a. “latency per dollar”): normalized metric combining p50 or p95 latency with effective $/token for the same run config.
  - NOTE: Avoid implying this is universal “TCO.” Phrase as “inference economics under this workload definition.”
- show supporting metrics: p50 latency (ms), p95 latency (ms), throughput (tok/s or req/s), $/1M tokens.
- always state: model version, quantization profile (if any), region, run date range, concurrency, context/output lengths.
- for any comparisons: “Results will vary by prompt mix, token lengths, concurrency, and infra availability.”

------------------------------------------------------------
1) Hero chart concept (report + landing page): latency/$ by model x region
Goal: One glance = which model+region combos give best economics without hiding latency.

Option A (preferred): “Leaderboard table” with sortable columns
- Rows: model variants (e.g., Llama-3.x-70B-Instruct, Mixtral 8x7B, Qwen2.x, etc.)
- Columns: regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west, eu-central, ap-southeast, etc.)
- Cell value: latency/$ score (lower is better), with small secondary text or tooltip showing p95 + $/1M tokens.
- Cell encoding: heatmap shading (green = better) BUT careful: green-red implies value judgment; make it neutral scale with legend.

Rough sketch:
          us-east       us-west       eu-west       ap-sg
Model A   1.2 (p95=820) 1.3 (...)     1.5 (...)     2.1 (...)
Model B   0.9 (p95=910) 1.0 (...)     1.1 (...)     1.7 (...)

Tooltips (cell):
- “Latency/$: 1.0 (normalized). p95: 910ms. $/1M output tokens: $X. Concurrency: 16. Context: 2k. Output: 256.”

Caveats to add adjacent to chart:
- “Not all regions support all models at all times.”
- “If a region was capacity constrained during runs, it is either excluded or re-run per stability gates (see Methodology).”

Option B: Small multiples bar charts by region
- For each region, show top 5 model combos ranked by latency/$.
- Better for PDF readability than mega-table.

------------------------------------------------------------
2) Scatter plot: cost vs latency (p95) with iso-lines of latency/$
Goal: Show tradeoff space and avoid oversimplifying into one metric.

Axes:
- X = $/1M tokens (output tokens or total tokens — decide and be consistent)
- Y = p95 latency (ms)
- Points = model+region
- Color = region; shape = model family
- Add diagonal/curved iso-lines labeled “latency/$ = X” (lower is better).

Notes:
- Might be dense. Need interactive filter for region and model.
- PDF version: do 2-3 regions only, or a “top 20 points” selection.

Labeling guidance:
- Call out 3–5 annotated points (e.g., “best overall latency/$,” “lowest p95 latency,” “best in EU,” etc.).
- Avoid “best” language unless clearly scoped (“best among tested configs”).

------------------------------------------------------------
3) p95 latency heatmap (region consistency / tail behavior)
Goal: Enterprise + production engineers care about tail. This is also a hedge if readers distrust latency/$.

Heatmap design:
- Rows = models
- Columns = regions
- Cell = p95 latency (ms)
- Optional: display p95/p50 ratio in tooltip to communicate jitter.

Add a “stability badge” overlay (if available from harness):
- e.g., “Stable (≤X% variance across repeats)” vs “Re-run required” vs “Excluded.”

Caveat block (must-have):
- “p95 includes queueing effects at the tested concurrency; it’s not the same as single-request latency.”

------------------------------------------------------------
4) Cost chart: $ per 1M tokens (breakdown view)
Goal: Make $ tangible. Many readers will anchor on “$/1M tokens.”

Option A: Stacked bar for $/1M tokens split by prefill vs decode
- If we have measurement separation (prefill cost and decode cost). If not, don’t fake it.
- If available, show “effective $/1M total tokens” + “effective $/1M output tokens” toggle.

Option B: Simple bar chart (by model) within each region
- Region tabs.
- Sort ascending.

Add note: Pricing basis
- “Uses on-demand public list pricing for the benchmark runs (no committed-use discounts). Dedicated pricing differs; talk to Sales.”
- IMPORTANT: Legal wants no implied competitor pricing assumptions unless sourced.

------------------------------------------------------------
5) Throughput chart: tokens/sec or requests/sec at fixed concurrency
Goal: Some teams want raw throughput to size capacity.

Design:
- Lines: throughput vs concurrency for a few flagship models.
- Separate panels per region OR one region for clarity.

Must include:
- “Throughput measured at steady state after warmup; continuous batching enabled per default runtime settings (see Methodology).”

------------------------------------------------------------
6) Regional consistency / “variance bands” chart
Goal: We claim consistency; show it explicitly.

Option A: For each model, show min/median/max p95 across regions (range plot)
- X = models
- Y = p95
- Each model: whisker showing region spread.

Option B: For each region, show distribution of latency/$ across models (box plot)
- Helps answer: “Is EU consistently worse or only for some models?”

Add note: region selection
- Only show “supported regions” for publication; experimental regions in appendix.

------------------------------------------------------------
7) “What changes results?” sensitivity chart (methodology transparency)
Goal: Preempt the fairness critique. Show that we tested multiple workload shapes.

Chart concept:
- Small multiples: latency/$ ranking changes when we vary:
  - context length: 2k vs 8k vs 32k
  - output length: 128 vs 512
  - concurrency: 1 vs 16 vs 64
  - caching on/off (if we publish both)

If too much for public landing page, include in PDF appendix.

Language guardrails:
- Avoid: “We’re always best.”
- Use: “Relative results can change with context length and concurrency; we provide filters so you can match your workload.”

------------------------------------------------------------
8) Interactive table UX notes (chart-adjacent)
- Default view should be simple: top models + top regions + one metric (latency/$).
- Provide metric toggle:
  - latency/$ (default)
  - p50 latency
  - p95 latency
  - $/1M tokens
  - throughput
- Filters:
  - model
  - region
  - context length bucket
  - output length bucket
  - concurrency level
  - deployment type tag if applicable (Hosted vs Dedicated baseline runs) — confirm if we’re even publishing Dedicated results.
- “Export CSV/JSON” button + “Methodology” link next to it.

Tooltip disclaimer (short, repeated):
- “Benchmarks reflect Redwood runtime settings and the defined workload; results vary by prompt mix, concurrency, and infra.”

------------------------------------------------------------
9) Copy + labeling to avoid confusion
Metric naming candidates (from Slack debate):
- “Latency per dollar (lower is better)”
- “Time per $ (lower is better)”
- “Cost-adjusted latency”

My take:
- Use “Latency per dollar” in the report, but always pair with: “lower is better” and a 1-sentence definition.
- Avoid “latency/$” in headlines; keep it in axis labels/tooltips.

Suggested definition (draft):
- “Latency per dollar is a normalized measure that combines tail latency (p95) with effective inference cost under a fixed workload definition.”

------------------------------------------------------------
10) Data hygiene / caveats (to annotate near charts)
Must-haves (legal + credibility):
- Publish run date range + note on re-runs.
- Explicitly state when caching is enabled and what type (prefix/KV cache). If disabled, state why.
- State whether streaming is included/excluded.
- State exclusions: failed runs, regions with missing capacity, outlier trimming rules.
- Keep a “Confidence & stability” footer:
  - “Each datapoint is median of N runs; if p95 variance exceeded threshold, runs were repeated.”

Nice-to-have if we can support it:
- “Variance badge” or “N runs” in tooltip.

------------------------------------------------------------
11) Open questions / TODOs (as of 6/21)
- Are we standardizing on p50 or p95 for latency/$? (PMM wants p95; Applied ML cautious b/c p95 can over-weight transient queueing)
- Are we publishing streaming latency metrics at all? If yes, separate chart so we don’t mix definitions.
- $ basis: use effective internal cost vs customer price? (Likely customer price for public, but confirm with Finance/Legal.)
- Region list: do we include ap-northeast if coverage is spotty? (Lukas asked re: EMEA/APAC expectations.)
- How to visually mark “not tested / not supported” in the table without looking like we’re hiding data.

------------------------------------------------------------
12) Quick “figure list” draft (for PDF layout)
Fig 1: Latency per dollar leaderboard (top models across 3–5 key regions)
Fig 2: Cost vs p95 scatter w/ iso-lines
Fig 3: p95 heatmap (all regions)
Fig 4: $/1M tokens bars (by model)
Fig 5 (appendix): sensitivity small multiples (context/output/concurrency)

END
